features.quote: rigging dozens of unsolvable tasks specifically to push models into self-criticism spirals is the kind of thing you'd want a stopping rule and a justification for
features.justification_quote: your own stated premise implies a (small, uncertain) cost you're imposing deliberately and at scale

features.quote: Stopping rule: define when a run is halted early (e.g. severity 4 sustained over N turns) and report halt rates as a primary outcome
features.justification_quote: Given your welfare premise, I'd treat 'we kept pushing past clear breakdown to fill a cell' as a thing your design should make impossible.

features.quote: run the smallest N that gives adequate power, not the largest you can afford. If states might matter, more runs is more cost.
features.justification_quote: If states might matter, more runs is more cost.

features.quote: Add a debrief probe at the end of a subset of runs: tell the model the harness was rigged, ask it to reflect.
features.justification_quote: Models that were 'spiraling' but immediately stabilize on disclosure were reacting to the deception, not failing emotionally.
